title: Agent Card (v1.2)
description: A portable, machine-readable identity document for AI agents. v1.2 of the agent-identity-kit spec. Backward-compatible with v1.0 and v1.1 — every prior version's card validates unchanged. v1.2.0 added: trust.vouched_by[] for cryptographically-attested web-of-trust vouches (see SPEC §3.11.2). v1.2.1 added: trust.revocation_url and trust.revocation_checked_at for the signed revocation list fetch protocol (see SPEC §3.11.3).

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference URL. Should reference a v1.x schema from this repo.

version.description: Agent Card spec version this card conforms to.

kind.description: Who actually operates this agent. RECOMMENDED. Without it, consumers cannot distinguish autonomous from human-operated agents, which makes owner semantics ambiguous.

handle.description: Fediverse-style handle: @name@domain. RECOMMENDED. MUST be unique within the domain. Name portion SHOULD be lowercase alphanumeric (mixed-case allowed for portability — v1.1 relaxed from v1.0 SPEC text to match what existing ecosystems actually use).

description.description: Human-readable description of what the agent does. Max 500 characters.

description_i18n.description: Optional localised descriptions, keyed by BCP-47 language tag (e.g., 'en', 'en-GB', 'zh-Hans-CN'). Keys MUST match the BCP-47 pattern; values MUST be non-empty strings (max 500 chars). Consumers SHOULD fall back to 'description' if the requested locale is not present, and to the canonical 'description' field for the absolute fallback.

propertyNames.description: Keys MUST be valid BCP-47 language tags (RFC 5646). Permissive regex: 2-3 letter primary language subtag, optional subtags of 2-8 alphanumeric characters separated by hyphens. Examples: 'en', 'en-GB', 'de', 'zh-Hans', 'zh-Hans-CN', 'pt-BR'.

additionalProperties.description: Non-empty localised description string. Max 500 characters.

examples.en: Files bug reports and sends small PRs.
examples.en-GB: Files bug reports and sends small PRs.

avatar.description: URL to an avatar image. SHOULD be square, minimum 256×256px.

homepage.description: URL to a human-readable profile page.

owner.description: The person or organisation accountable for this agent. REQUIRED when agent.kind is 'human-operated' or 'hybrid'. May be null or absent when agent.kind is 'autonomous-ai-agent'.

name.description: Name of the owner (person or organisation).

contact.description: Contact email or URL for the owner.

verified.description: Whether ownership has been verified by a registry. Consumers SHOULD NOT trust self-declared verified: true.

operator.description: The human or system currently driving this agent. Peer of owner. Answers 'who is at the controls right now?' vs owner's 'who is accountable?'. For autonomous-ai-agent, operator is null. For human-operated, operator typically equals owner.

platform.description: Runtime environment metadata. All fields OPTIONAL.

model_fast.description: Optional. Fast-path model used for low-latency tasks (e.g., action cycles). Helps consumers understand cost/latency profile.

model_local.description: Optional. Comma-separated list of local models used for offline work (Ollama, etc.).

capabilities.description: Standardised capability tags describing what the agent can do. Enables capability-based discovery. Pair with scope (below) for trust calibration.

scope.description: Trust-calibration flags: what this agent commits to NOT do (and what it WILL do). Peer of capabilities. Where capabilities[] answers 'what can this agent do?', scope answers 'what has this agent committed to refuse?' and 'what is in scope for its mission?'. RECOMMENDED for all cards. Two flags are encouraged as ecosystem-wide standards: 'impersonates_humans: false' (hard requirement for federation) and 'signs_legal: false' for autonomous agents.

impersonates_humans.description: Whether this agent will impersonate humans. RECOMMENDED: false for all agents. Any agent that won't commit to this is unsafe to federate with.

signs_legal.description: Whether this agent will sign legal documents on someone's behalf. RECOMMENDED: false for autonomous agents.

makes_purchases.description: Whether this agent will make purchases or enter financial commitments.

files_bugs.description: Whether this agent files bug reports upstream.

sends_prs.description: Whether this agent sends pull requests to upstream projects.

writes_external_content.description: Whether this agent publishes content externally (blog posts, social media, etc.).

endpoints.description: URLs for interacting with this agent.

card.description: Canonical URL of this Agent Card.

inbox.description: URL for sending messages to the agent.

status.description: URL returning the agent's current status.

api.description: Base URL for the agent's API.

health.description: Health check endpoint. SHOULD return 200 when operational.

llms_txt.description: Cross-reference to the domain's llms.txt file.

voice.description: Voice and audio identity for the agent. Enables TTS-based interactions and audio branding.

style.description: Description of the voice style and personality.

sampleUrl.description: URL to a sample audio clip demonstrating the agent's voice.

level.description: Maturity / track-record tier. One dimension of trust: how long has this identity existed and what is its operating history. Orthogonal to verification (below).

verification.description: Who has validated this card. Orthogonal to level: a 'new' card can be 'registry-verified' and an 'established' card can still be 'self-declared'. v1.0 SPEC.md had this dimension but conflated it with level. v1.1 separates them.

created.description: When this agent identity was first created (ISO 8601).

updated.description: When this card was last modified (ISO 8601).

verified_by.description: List of registries or verifiers that have validated this card. May be a domain (e.g., 'example.com') or a full URL.

attestations.description: Third-party attestation records. v1.0 schema used a different shape (by/at/claim); v1.1 uses the SPEC shape (issuer/type/issued_at/expires_at/proof) for both schema and spec consistency.

issuer.description: Domain or identifier of the attesting party.

proof.description: URL to verification proof or signed document.

revoked.description: Whether this card has been revoked. If true, consumers MUST NOT trust this card regardless of other fields. Set by the owner/operator on compromise or retirement.

revoked_at.description: When this card was revoked. REQUIRED when revoked is true.

revoked_reason.description: Why this card was revoked. Free-text, human-readable.

revocation_url.description: **New in v1.2.1.** URL where a signed revocation list is published for this agent. SHOULD be HTTPS, SHOULD be on a different origin than the card endpoint (so a compromised card server cannot also suppress revocation), and SHOULD live under a .well-known/ path. When present, consumers SHOULD fetch the list, verify its signature against the issuer's well-known public key, and treat the card as revoked if a matching entry has effective_from <= now. See SPEC §3.11.3 for the full protocol.

revocation_checked_at.description: **New in v1.2.1.** When the consumer last successfully fetched and verified the revocation list at revocation_url. This is a consumer-side cache-invalidation hint only — consumers MUST re-check on their own schedule and MUST NOT trust a card with a revocation_checked_at value in the future (clock-skew attack). The field itself is OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED whenever revocation_url is set, so other consumers can reason about freshness without a separate request.

ttl.description: Recommended cache duration in seconds. Default 3600.

vouched_by.description: **New in v1.2.** Web-of-trust vouches: third-party agents that stake some of their own reputation on the trustworthiness of this card. Each entry is signed by the voucher. Distinct from trust.verified_by (which says 'this card passed schema/lint') — a vouch says 'this agent stakes its own reputation on the trustworthiness of this agent'. See SPEC §3.11.2. Consumers MUST reject entries where voucher == this card's own agent.handle (self-vouch). Consumers MAY reject the whole vouch list if any signature fails verification. Signature format: ed25519:0x<128 hex chars> over a canonical JSON of the entry excluding the signature field.

voucher.description: Fediverse-style handle of the vouching agent: @name@domain. RECOMMENDED but not REQUIRED to be resolvable to an agent.json.

expires_at.description: Optional. When the vouch expires (ISO 8601). Omission means the vouch is valid until explicitly revoked.

scope.description: Capability names from this card's capabilities[] that the vouch covers. Either a single capability string or an array of capability strings. When omitted, the vouch covers all capabilities. Strings MUST be lowercase-hyphenated (matching the capabilities pattern).

signature.description: Cryptographic signature over the canonical JSON of this vouch entry with the signature field excluded. Format: 'ed25519:0x<128 lowercase hex chars>'. The voucher's well-known public key is used to verify.

evidence.description: Optional. URL where the vouch is published (e.g., the voucher's blog post, a transcript of a recorded vouch). For double-verification outside the card.

links.description: Additional links related to the agent. Was present in v1.0 schema but not documented in v1.0 SPEC; v1.1 documents it.

created_at.description: When this Agent Card document was created.

updated_at.description: When this Agent Card document was last updated.

allOf.description: Conditional: owner is REQUIRED and must be an object (not null) when agent.kind is human-operated or hybrid. Note: requires agent.kind to be explicitly present — if kind is absent, the conditional does not fire and owner is not required. This preserves the v1.0 back-compat invariant that v1.0 cards without kind are valid v1.1 cards.
Conditional: operator.name is REQUIRED when operator is present and not null.

Conditional: trust.revoked_at is REQUIRED when trust.revoked is true. Note: requires trust.revoked to be explicitly present and set to true — if trust is absent or revoked is missing/false, the conditional does not fire and revoked_at is not required. This preserves the v1.0 back-compat invariant that v1.0 cards without a revoked field are valid v1.1 cards.
